proof.label: Sample

reviews.text: We live in Eastwood in a 1920s house with slanted ceilings upstairs. They knew the layout before they climbed in: knee walls, the little attic above, then the floor behind. Warmer and quieter.
reviews.name: Paula D.
reviews.service: Knee walls in city frame houses

reviews.text: After a big lake-effect week our roof had a ridge of ice along the gutter. They found the leaks around the old chimney chase and the ceiling lights. This February the snow sat evenly.
reviews.name: Joe C.

reviews.text: Tipp Hill, narrow lot, clapboard I did not want ruined. The holes they drilled for dense-pack are plugged and painted, and I have to look hard to find them.
reviews.name: Siobhan R.

reviews.text: Our colonial had a cold strip of floor along every outside wall. Foam on the rim joist in the basement fixed it in a day, and the basement was swept when they left.
reviews.name: Ray T.

reviews.text: The kitchen sits over what used to be a porch and the tile was icy every winter. They went in from below, sealed it and insulated it. Slippers optional now.
reviews.name: Dana F.

reviews.text: Clear about what was worth doing and what was not. They told us the attic was mostly fine and the real problem was the hatch and the bath fan. Small bill, big difference upstairs.
reviews.name: Megan H.

proof.guarantee: If the snow on your roof still melts in stripes over a spot we sealed, we come back that winter and fix it.

prices.note: to the typical R-49 to R-60 range
